subject: Interop bench runway: p95/p99 A-B plan & access
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Alex Carter <alex.carter@stratusai.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-28T16:12:00-08:00
Subject: Interop bench runway: p95/p99 A-B plan & access

Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for your time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we're all aligned before the lab run: 

Summary of call:
- Goal: direct comparative sweep between Redwood Inference and the hyperscaler endpoint you mentioned (primary focus: p95/p99 latency and sustained tokens/sec under production-like load).
- Scope: Chat generation workload + long-context retrieval path that exercises KV cache warm/cold behavior.
- Success signals: p95 < target for each experiment (we'll set target per test), stable throughput in tokens/sec across sustained 10m windows, and consistent top-k output similarity on a small eval set.

Immediate asks from your side:
1) Access to a small sample trace or representative request file (500-1,000 requests). You mentioned a Drive folder — we'll use that for ingestion.
2) Clarify whether comparison should include the hyperscaler with dynamic autoscaling or a pinned-reserved endpoint.
3) Any SLA-ish thresholds that would be deal blockers (e.g., hard p99 max).

Proposed A/B test matrix (high-level):
- Workloads: short prompt (64 tokens), medium (256 tokens), long (1,024 tokens).
- Modes: cold-start (empty KV), warm-path (KV warmed), streaming vs non-streaming responses.
- Concurrency sweep: 1, 8, 32, 128 concurrent requests; capture request-level latencies and system-level tokens/sec for sustained 10m windows.
- Metrics we will report: p50/p95/p99, mean latency, tokens/sec, tail error rate, CPU/GPU utilization, and cost-tokens estimate.

Attachments included: redwood-bench-plan-v2.pdf (detailed test matrix) and 20261128_stratus_bench_samples.csv (request samples format). Please review the plan and tell us which test cells you care most about so we can prioritize the first runs.

Next proposed milestones:
- Nov 30: test window (we can run midday PST); confirm access by EOD Nov 29.
- Dec 1: deliver preliminary comparison dashboard and a short scorecard.

Jonas is looped in for runtime/kernel questions; Dylan will own the run coordination. If you prefer, we can run a short sanity A/B (512-token medium prompt, 32 concurrency) first to validate traces.

Thanks — looking forward to running this.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
T: +1 (415) 555-0148

Attachments: redwood-bench-plan-v2.pdf (see test matrix), 20261128_stratus_bench_samples.csv (sample requests)
From: Alex Carter <alex.carter@stratusai.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya@stratusai.com>
Date: 2026-11-28T18:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Interop bench runway: p95/p99 A-B plan & access

Thanks Tessa — helpful recap. A couple quick clarifications from our side: 

1) We'll start with a pinned-reserved endpoint on the hyperscaler side to keep instance variability out of the first comparison. If later you want to see autoscale effects we can add a second pass.
2) Our initial pass should prioritize medium and long contexts (256 and 1,024 tokens) — we care most about tail latency for longer prompts.
3) For data access, I've uploaded 800 sample requests to the Drive link you referenced (file name: stratus_samples_800.jsonl). I'll grant your team viewer access and can create an S3 read key if you prefer direct pull.

Two questions for your engineers: what exact GPU types will you use for Redwood runs? Also, can you confirm we capture both cold-start 95/99 (first token) and steady-state token emission rates? We want tokens/sec as a primary throughput metric.

Availability: Nov 30 afternoon PST works for a live run — we'll shadow and provide immediate feedback.

Alex
Director of Platform Engineering
StratusAI

Date: 2026-11-29T09:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Interop bench runway: p95/p99 A-B plan & access

Alex / Priya —

Thanks for the upload and the pinned-reserved clarification. Quick technical plan and what we'll capture during the run: 

Planned runtime for Redwood runs:
- GPU profile: Ampere A10G equivalent for parity with your hyperscaler reserved instance (will note exact SKU in final report).
- Runtime flags: quantization profile Q4_0 for medium/large runs; exact kernel set and batching policy logged per experiment.

Test cells we'll execute (priority order):
1) Medium prompt (256 tokens), concurrency 32, compare cold-start p95/p99 and warm-path p95/p99. Capture tokens/sec over 10m sustained window.
2) Long prompt (1,024 tokens), concurrency 8 and 32. Capture tail latency and tokens/sec.
3) Streaming vs non-streaming for the 512-token sanity run if we need to validate emission behavior.

Metrics capture details:
- Per-request timestamps for first token emitted and final token emitted (to compute p95/p99 first-token latency and end-to-end).
- Tokens/sec computed as total tokens emitted / wall-clock of the 10m window. We'll also report tokens/sec per-GPU to normalize.
- Resource telemetry: GPU util, memory, kernel stalls (where available).
- Quality check: run 50 eval prompts through both systems and compute token-level edit distance and a small human-review scorecard for hallucination/regression.

Canary A/B plan: For each cell we'll run alternating 5-minute buckets (Redwood / Hyperscaler) for the first 30 minutes to get live comparison while keeping cluster reuse minimal. If you want fully isolated runs (no reuse), say so — it will increase run time but gives purer cold-start signals.

Jonas will instrument the runtime for low-level traces if we hit unexpected tails. If you can share an S3 role or pre-signed URLs for the sample file we'll pull those directly to the runner.

I attached the updated bench plan (redwood-bench-plan-v2.pdf) which includes exact CLI commands and the JSON schema we expect for samples. We'll capture raw traces and a condensed CSV with per-request latencies.

Dylan
Senior Benchmark Engineer, Redwood Inference

Perfect — appreciate the quick turnaround on samples and the pinned-reserved note. Next steps from here: 

1) Please add read access on the Drive folder for tessa.morgan@redwood.com and dylan.brooks@redwood.com, or drop an S3 presigned URL for stratus_samples_800.jsonl. We'll pull the file and validate schema by EOD Nov 29.
2) We'll run the sanity 512-token sanity A/B at 12:00 PM PST on Nov 30, then proceed with the prioritized medium and long cells. Expect ~90 minutes for the prioritized sweep (with alternating 5-minute canary buckets).
3) We'll send an interim dashboard link and a short scorecard within 24 hours of the run. If anything looks off on tail error rates or p99, Jonas will reach out immediately and we can schedule a deep-dive.

Jonas — can you be on standby at noon PST for kernel-level questions?

Alex / Priya — if the pinned-reserved hyperscaler instance SKU is available for the run, please share the SKU so we can match GPU memory and clock characteristics.

Thanks again — excited to get this data in hand.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
